page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 7.75 GB per core. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz, the instance features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and int8 operations. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks reveal a strong divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier single-core performance in Geekbench and text processing, as well as strong single-threaded compression and decompression rates. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks are relatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier results in stress-ng multi-core tests, Passmark CPU scores, and large-block memory read/write bandwidth. Static web serving throughput and small-model LLM inference speeds remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-4 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound applications that do not require massive parallel processing. The instance is well-suited for single-threaded text processing, memory-intensive caching, lightweight database operations, and small-scale language model inference.
